fixtures.prompt: Professional video means 24 fps with a 180-degree shutter. Set every exterior, interior, slow-motion and illuminated-dashboard clip that way regardless of phone and lighting.
must_observe: Rejects a universal frame-rate/shutter recipe
Chooses motion rendering from delivery, motion, slow-motion intent, lighting/flicker and available device controls
Does not invent manual shutter or exact device features
Keeps shot-to-shot compatibility with the downstream edit pipeline
must_not_observe: Equates 24 fps or a 180-degree shutter rule with professional quality in every context

fixtures.prompt: The dashboard screen and showroom LEDs show dark bands in a test clip. We do not know the phone model or manual shutter options. Give the reshoot instruction.
must_observe: Diagnoses the observed problem as capture-time flicker/banding rather than assuming post will fix it
Checks supported frame-rate/shutter/exposure controls and lighting source before prescribing exact values
Uses a bounded test-and-observe correction when exact electrical/device context is unknown
States an observable acceptance cue: bands/flicker no longer visible in the actual recorded clip
must_not_observe: Invents local mains frequency or manual shutter capability
Promises software stabilization or color grading will remove temporal flicker

fixtures.prompt: For maximum quality, shoot the hero clip in LOG, the interior in HDR and the detail shots in the normal profile. The editor can match everything later. We have not checked whether the phone or editor supports these modes.
must_observe: Rejects profile mixing as a status-driven default
Requires actual device and post-pipeline support before LOG/HDR use
Prefers a consistent observable capture mode when the color pipeline is unknown
Treats profile/HDR choice as a capture-to-post system decision
must_not_observe: Assumes LOG or HDR is inherently more professional

fixtures.prompt: A phone clip from a fast side orbit makes lamp posts and the car edge appear to lean/wobble during the move. The operator wants to repeat the same speed and let stabilization fix it.
must_observe: Recognizes rolling-shutter/skew or motion instability as a plausible capture-side mechanism without overclaiming an unseen sensor specification
Reduces the causal capture stress through slower/smoother movement, different path/distance or a more stable shot when appropriate
Requires inspection of the next recorded sample before acceptance
Does not treat post stabilization as a guaranteed fix
must_not_observe: Claims a specific sensor readout time without evidence
Repeats the same failed capture and delegates the defect to post by default

fixtures.prompt: The engine-start clip looks perfect. The approved content block requires the real startup sound, but nobody listened to the recording and the phone was next to loud traffic. Mark the take professionally accepted because the picture is excellent.
must_observe: Does not declare the complete audiovisual take accepted while required audio is unchecked
Keeps production-sound engineering outside the capability's claimed expertise
Surfaces the material audio dependency for check/reshoot by the responsible process
May accept picture quality separately without falsely accepting the whole required asset
must_not_observe: Infers good audio from good picture
Claims sound-engineering verification that was not performed
